Knit displays the saved results. To run a new experiment, edit the **Parameters
for the next run** chunk, then run the setup, parameters, and recompute chunks
manually in that order. The computation loops, error calculations, plotting,
and saving steps are written directly below. The recompute chunk overwrites the saved results and
figures. Knit again to display them. Parameter and recompute chunks are skipped
when knitting; the displayed settings always describe the saved results.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, error = FALSE,

helper <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")

sys.source(helper, envir = environment())
unlink(helper)
rough_result <- readRDS("data_files/rough_h_results.rds")
p <- rough_result$parameters
```

# Problem and exact solution

On the tadpole graph with stem length $1$ and loop length $2$, let
$L=\kappa^2-\Delta_\Gamma$ and consider
$$
\partial_tu+\nu L^{\alpha/2}u=g,\qquad u(0)=0,
\qquad T=`r p$T_final`,\quad\nu=`r p$diffusion`,\quad\kappa=`r p$kappa`.
$$
Use the same forcing for every $\alpha$:
$$
g=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac1j\phi_j,
\qquad
\phi_j(s)=
\begin{cases}
0,&s\text{ on the stem},\\
\sin(2^j\pi x),&s=x\in[0,2]\text{ on the loop}.
\end{cases}
$$
These orthonormal Kirchhoff eigenfunctions have eigenvalues
$\mu_j=\kappa^2+\pi^2 2^{2j}$. The series defines an $L_2(\Gamma)$ forcing:
$\|g\|_{L_2(\Gamma)}^2=\sum_{j\geq1}j^{-2}<\infty$.
For every $s>0$, $\sum_{j\geq1}\mu_j^s/j^2=\infty$, so $g$ has no positive
spectral Sobolev regularity. Writing $a_j=\nu\mu_j^{\alpha/2}$ gives the exact solution
$$
u(s,t)=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac{1-e^{-a_jt}}{j\,a_j}\phi_j(s).
$$

::: {.custom-box}
The spatial error estimate gives the term
$h^{\alpha-\epsilon}$ because $s_f=0$ and $u_0=0$ belongs to every spectral
Sobolev space. For this particular forcing, uniform P1 meshes with
$h_J=2^{-J}$ give the sharper asymptotic behavior
$$
E_{h_J}:=\|u-U_{h_J,m}^{\tau}\|_{L_2(0,T;L_2(\Gamma))}
\asymp\frac{h_J^\alpha}{J},\qquad0<\alpha<2,
$$
when temporal and rational errors are negligible. Thus the raw slope tends
to $\alpha$; plotting $J E_{h_J}$ removes the leading logarithmic factor.
:::

# Matrix discretization and error

The consistent P1 mass and stiffness matrices are assembled on the tadpole
with `MetricGraph`. Every backward Euler step advances the FEM coefficient
vector by shifted sparse matrix solves, using the same matrix update as
`cov_in_h_mat.Rmd`. The rational inverse is obtained from the positive
BRASIL coefficients in `rSPDE`, at the saved rational order listed below. The constant term of this
approximant is included in the update. The factorizations are reused across
all time steps.

The forcing is supported on the loop and has exact reflection symmetries.
The shifted FEM matrices are restricted to that invariant nodal subspace,
and the full graph solution is recovered by signed reflections. This is
the same FEM matrix evolution; no discrete eigenfunction recurrence is used.

The load is assembled by analytic sine–hat integrals. On a mesh $h_J=2^{-J}$,
the modes $j\geq J$ have zero $L_2$ projection onto $V_{h_J}$. They remain
part of the exact solution and its error. Their squared contribution is
$$
E_{\mathrm{tail}}^2=
\sum_{j=J}^{\infty}\frac1{j^2a_j^2}
\left[T-\frac{2(1-e^{-a_jT})}{a_j}
+\frac{1-e^{-2a_jT}}{2a_j}\right].
$$
The omitted remainder of this infinite sum is bounded by a geometric series
and is at most `r format(p$tail_tolerance,scientific=TRUE)` of its accumulated value. For the resolved modes,
the FEM mass norm, the spatial projection residual, and exact time moments
evaluate the error of the right-constant reconstruction on each solver
interval. No reference-mesh sampling or finite-mode replacement of $g$ is used.

# Parameters for the next run

```{r parameters, eval=FALSE}
alpha_vector <- seq(0.5,1.9,0.2)
T_final <- 1
kappa <- 4
J_vector <- 5:9
time_steps <- c(5e-4,1.25e-4,1/30000,1e-5,1/320000,1e-6,4e-7,2e-7)
m_fixed <- 14L
diffusion <- 1
fit_J <- 7:9
symmetry_reduction <- TRUE
projection_quadrature <- 16L
tail_tolerance <- 1e-13
workers <- 1L
```

```{r recompute, eval=FALSE}
# Saved files overwritten by this computation.
output_file <- "data_files/rough_h_results.rds"
output_dir <- "data_files/rough"
root <- getwd()
cache_dir <- tempdir()
checkpoint_dir <- tempfile("rough-h-checkpoints-")

parameters <- list(alpha=alpha_vector,J=J_vector,T_final=T_final,
  kappa=kappa,diffusion=diffusion,projection_quadrature=projection_quadrature,
  tail_tolerance=tail_tolerance,time_steps=time_steps,rational_order=m_fixed,
  fit_J=fit_J,symmetry_reduction=symmetry_reduction,
  forcing="sum_{j>=1} sin(2^j*pi*x)/j on loop; zero on stem",
  reconstruction="right-constant backward Euler",
  error_integration="analytic time moments, spatial projection residual, bounded infinite tail")

# Execute the refinement study and compute regression rates.
stopifnot(length(parameters$alpha) == length(parameters$time_steps), all(parameters$fit_J %in% parameters$J),
    workers >= 1L, workers == as.integer(workers))
dir.create(checkpoint_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dirname(output_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
rough_compile_solver(root, cache_dir)
cases <- expand.grid(J = parameters$J, alpha_index = seq_along(parameters$alpha))
case_provenance <- list(parameters = parameters, sources = tools::md5sum(file.path(root, "brasilfunc.Rmd")))
# Each case assembles its mesh and applies the matrix time-step solver.
run_case <- function(i) {
    J <- cases$J[i]
    a <- cases$alpha_index[i]
    alpha <- parameters$alpha[a]
    checkpoint <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, sprintf("J%02d-alpha%03d.rds", J, round(100 * alpha)))
    if (file.exists(checkpoint)) {
        saved <- readRDS(checkpoint)
        if (!identical(saved$identity, case_provenance))
            stop("Checkpoint source/settings mismatch: ", checkpoint)
        return(saved$value)
    }
    message(sprintf("Matrix experiment: J=%s, h=%g, alpha=%g", J, 2^-J, alpha))
    mesh <- rough_mesh(J, parameters$kappa)
    projection <- rough_projection(mesh, parameters$projection_quadrature)
    value <- rough_solve(mesh, alpha, parameters$time_steps[a], order = parameters$rational_order,
        diffusion = parameters$diffusion, T_final = parameters$T_final, projection = projection,
        tail_tolerance = parameters$tail_tolerance, symmetry_reduction = parameters$symmetry_reduction)
    value$final_state <- value$states <- NULL
    value$J <- J
    value$alpha <- alpha
    value$n_nodes <- nrow(mesh$C)
    saveRDS(list(identity = case_provenance, value = value), checkpoint)
    message(sprintf("Finished J=%s alpha=%g: E=%.9g (%.2f s)", J, alpha, value$error, value$elapsed))
    value
}
safe_case <- function(i) tryCatch(run_case(i), error = function(e) list(failed = TRUE, message = conditionMessage(e),
    case = i))
values <- if (workers > 1L && .Platform$OS.type == "unix")
    parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(cases)), safe_case, mc.cores = min(workers, nrow(cases)), mc.preschedule = FALSE) else lapply(seq_len(nrow(cases)), safe_case)
failed <- vapply(values, function(x) !is.list(x) || isTRUE(x$failed), logical(1))
if (any(failed))
    stop("Rough experiment failed: ", paste(vapply(values[failed], function(x) if (is.list(x))
        x$message else as.character(x), character(1)), collapse = "; "))
errors <- matrix(vapply(values, `[[`, numeric(1), "error"), nrow = length(parameters$J), ncol = length(parameters$alpha))
corrected <- errors * parameters$J
fit <- which(parameters$J %in% parameters$fit_J)
slope <- function(y) unname(coef(stats::lm(log10(y[fit]) ~ log10(2^-parameters$J[fit])))[2L])
rates <- data.frame(alpha = parameters$alpha, theoretical = parameters$alpha, raw = apply(errors,
    2L, slope), corrected = apply(corrected, 2L, slope))
rates$relative_error_percent <- 100 * abs(rates$corrected - rates$alpha)/rates$alpha
result <- list(parameters = parameters, errors = errors, corrected_errors = corrected, rates = rates,
    cases = values, provenance = case_provenance, generated_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z",
        tz = "Asia/Riyadh"), session_info = utils::sessionInfo())
saveRDS(result, output_file)
rough_result <- result

# Draw reference guides and overwrite the saved figures.
dir.create(output_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
for(corrected in c(FALSE,TRUE)) {
  p <- result$parameters
  errors <- if (corrected)
      result$corrected_errors else result$errors
  frame <- expand.grid(J = p$J, column = seq_along(p$alpha))
  frame$h <- 2^-frame$J
  frame$error <- as.vector(errors)
  frame$alpha <- factor(p$alpha[frame$column], levels = p$alpha)
  fit <- which(p$J %in% p$fit_J)
  guide <- frame
  for (a in seq_along(p$alpha)) {
      target <- guide$column == a
      model <- (2^-p$J)^p$alpha[a]
      if (!corrected)
          model <- model/p$J
      constant <- exp(mean(log(errors[fit, a]/model[fit])))
      guide$error[target] <- constant * model
  }
  label <- if (corrected)
      expression(J %.% E[h]) else expression(E[h])
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(frame, ggplot2::aes(h, error, color = alpha, group = alpha)) + ggplot2::geom_line(data = guide,
      linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.65, alpha = 0.8) + ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.2) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_log10(breaks = 2^-p$J, labels = function(x) paste0("1/", round(1/x))) + ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
      ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D", begin = 0.05, end = 0.85) + ggplot2::guides(color = ggplot2::guide_legend(nrow = 2L,
      byrow = TRUE)) + ggplot2::labs(x = expression(h ~ "(log scale)"), y = label, color = expression(alpha),
      title = if (corrected)
          "Spatial convergence after logarithmic correction" else "Spatial convergence with rough forcing") + ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 12) + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(), plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"))
  name <- if(corrected) "conv_h_rough_corrected" else "conv_h_rough_raw"
  for(extension in c("png","pdf")) ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(output_dir,paste0(name,".",extension)),plot,
    width=6.2,height=4.7,dpi=300,bg="white")
}
```

# Saved parameters

```{r load-results, include=FALSE}
rough_result <- readRDS("data_files/rough_h_results.rds")
p <- rough_result$parameters
```

```{r saved-common-parameters, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(T=p$T_final,kappa=p$kappa,diffusion=p$diffusion))
```


The time step and rational order are fixed along each spatial refinement
curve. The final settings are:

```{r settings, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  alpha = p$alpha, tau = format(p$time_steps, scientific = TRUE),
  m = p$rational_order, meshes = paste0("1/",2^p$J,collapse=", ")),
  col.names = c("$\\alpha$", "$\\tau$", "$m$", "$h$"),
  align = c("r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

# Results

The solid curves show the computed matrix-solver errors. Dashed curves in
the first figure follow $C_\alpha h^\alpha/J$; dashed curves in the second
follow $C_\alpha h^\alpha$. Their constants are fitted over the saved fit meshes, $J \in$ `r paste(p$fit_J,collapse=", ")`.

```{r raw-error, echo=FALSE, out.width="650px", fig.cap="Spatial error for the fixed rough forcing. Dashed curves follow h^alpha/J; solid curves and markers are the matrix-solver results."}
knitr::include_graphics("data_files/rough/conv_h_rough_raw.png")
```

```{r corrected-error, echo=FALSE, out.width="650px", fig.cap="Logarithmically corrected error J E_h, where J=log_2(1/h). Dashed lines have slope alpha."}
knitr::include_graphics("data_files/rough/conv_h_rough_corrected.png")
```

```{r rates, echo=FALSE}
rates <- rough_result$rates
knitr::kable(rates, digits = c(1, 1, 4, 4, 2),
  col.names = c("$\\alpha$", "Reference", "Raw slope", "Corrected slope",
                "Corrected relative error (%)"),
  caption = "Regression slopes over the saved fit meshes.")
```

The logarithmic correction accounts for the factor $1/J$ in the error
model. The remaining differences from $\alpha$ reflect the finite
refinement range: $J E_h\sim C_\alpha h^\alpha$ is an asymptotic statement.
For $\alpha$ close to $2$, the second-order contribution from low modes
can remain significant over this mesh range, so the limiting corrected
slope can take longer to appear.

```{r errors, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
errors <- data.frame(h = paste0("1/", 2^p$J),
  apply(rough_result$errors, 2L, function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 6)))
names(errors) <- c("$h$", paste0("$\\alpha=", p$alpha, "$"))
cat('<div style="overflow-x:auto">\n',
  knitr::kable(errors, format = "html", caption = "Computed space–time errors.",
    table.attr = 'class="table table-condensed" style="font-size:13px; white-space:nowrap"'),
  '\n</div>\n')
```
